title: Spline IK Snake Locomotion Simulator
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a Spline IK snake locomotion simulator on a ground plane.

## Scene Setup
- Dark green ground plane (100x100 units) with a subtle grid overlay.
- Ambient light (intensity 0.4) + directional light from (5,10,5) casting soft shadows.
- Camera: perspective, FOV 55, positioned at (0, 18, 25) looking at origin. OrbitControls enabled.
- Sky-blue background color (#87CEEB).

## Snake Construction (Spline IK Chain)
- The snake is composed of exactly 16 spherical bone segments (radius 0.4 each), colored in a gradient from dark green (head, segment 0) to yellow-green (tail, segment 15).
- Segments are connected by a Catmull-Rom spline that passes through all segment centers. Render the spline as a TubeGeometry (radius 0.35, 128 tubular segments) with a semi-transparent green material so the bone spheres are visible inside.
- The head segment (index 0) is slightly larger (radius 0.55) and colored bright red.
- Each segment's Y position should be 0.4 (resting on the ground plane).
- Initial positions: all segments lined up along the negative Z axis, spaced 1.2 units apart. Head at (0, 0.4, 0), segment 1 at (0, 0.4, -1.2), etc.

## Locomotion Physics
- Implement serpentine (lateral undulation) locomotion. The head follows a target point. Each subsequent segment follows the one ahead of it using a follow-the-leader IK approach:
  - Each segment moves toward the position of the segment ahead, maintaining a fixed spacing of 1.2 units (tolerance ±0.05).
  - The spline is rebuilt every frame from the updated segment positions.
- The snake's head movement is driven by a sine-based lateral oscillation superimposed on the forward direction:
  - lateralOffset = sin(time * frequency) * amplitude
  - Default frequency: 2.0 Hz, default amplitude: 2.5 units
- Forward speed default: 3.0 units/second.
- The total body length (sum of distances between consecutive segments) must be conserved within ±0.5 units of the initial total length (18.0 units for 15 gaps × 1.2).

## User Interactions

### Keyboard Controls
- W/S: Increase/decrease forward speed by 0.5 units/s (clamp to [0.0, 8.0]).
- A/D: Steer the snake head direction left/right by rotating heading angle ±5 degrees per press.
- Q/E: Increase/decrease oscillation amplitude by 0.25 (clamp to [0.5, 5.0]).
- 1/2: Increase/decrease oscillation frequency by 0.25 Hz (clamp to [0.5, 5.0]).
- Space: Toggle pause/resume of the simulation.
- R: Reset snake to initial straight-line configuration, reset heading to 0, speed to 3.0, amplitude to 2.5, frequency to 2.0.
- U: Undo last parameter change (maintain a history stack of up to 20 parameter snapshots: speed, amplitude, frequency, heading).

### DOM Controls
- A HUD panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text) showing:
  - Current speed, amplitude, frequency, heading (degrees), paused state, total body length, frame count.
- A button labeled 'Toggle Skeleton' that shows/hides the bone spheres (tube always visible).
- A button labeled 'Toggle Trail' that enables/disables a trail effect: a fading line behind the head showing the last 200 head positions.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- segmentCount: number (always 16)
- segments: array of {x, y, z} for each segment center
- headPosition: {x, y, z} of segment 0
- tailPosition: {x, y, z} of segment 15
- speed: current forward speed (number)
- amplitude: current oscillation amplitude (number)
- frequency: current oscillation frequency (number)
- headingDeg: current heading in degrees (number)
- paused: boolean
- totalBodyLength: number (sum of consecutive segment distances)
- skeletonVisible: boolean
- trailEnabled: boolean
- trailPointCount: number (how many points currently in trail)
- frameCount: number (incremented each animation frame, paused frames still count)
- undoStackSize: number
- segmentSpacings: array of 15 numbers (distance between consecutive segments)
- splinePointCount: number (number of points sampled on the rendered spline tube)

Ensure all numerical values are never NaN or Infinity. The simulation should start automatically (not paused).
physics_constraints: 1. Segment spacing conservation: each consecutive pair must maintain 1.2 ± 0.05 unit distance. 2. Total body length conservation: sum of 15 spacings must remain 18.0 ± 0.5 units. 3. All segments must remain on the ground plane (Y ≈ 0.4 ± 0.1). 4. Head lateral oscillation must follow sin(t * freq) * amp pattern. 5. Speed, amplitude, frequency must stay within their clamped ranges. 6. No NaN or Infinity in any state field.
